key_insight: The paper introduces a simulation-free way to learn population dynamics directly in Wasserstein space, making it possible to model both dissipative and conservative/periodic evolution from snapshots alone. It replaces expensive per-training-step numerical solving with a residual-based learning objective.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing and forecasting how distributions of cells, organisms, or fluids evolve over time when only unpaired snapshots are available. Existing Wasserstein gradient-flow methods miss conservative or periodic behavior, and Lagrangian approaches have been simulation-based and costly to train.
method: Formulate learning as a Wasserstein Lagrangian residual problem, allowing dynamics to be learned without running a simulator inside training.
Use snapshot data to infer the underlying transport dynamics in probability space rather than tracking individual trajectories.
Extend modeling beyond gradient flows so the method can represent both dissipative and conservative/oscillatory processes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more scalable and flexible way to model time-evolving distributions from sparse observations. It broadens the class of dynamics that can be learned while reducing computational overhead during training.
